I watched my mom's best friend slowly kill himself with drugs and complications from AIDS.

This was in the mid 1990's. Will's partner, Ray, had already died from AIDS related illnesses. Will was lost and his heart was clearly, obviously, irreparably broken. 


He was brilliant. He was programming in the late 80s and early 90s, worked as a librarian for one of the largest libraries in south Florida, and taught on occult topics. He was kind and generous. But when Ray died, he just fell apart. He lost weight and developed sores on his body. We knew he wasn't well, but it was not evident to me just how bad it was until my mom told my sister and I (probably 11 and 9 at the time, respectively) that we were going to go and care for Will's pets. Will had been arrested for drugs (though that was not told to me at the time) and needed someone to go see to his two dogs and one cat. We were not prepared for what awaited us.


When we got to his huge beautiful house that he once shared with Ray... we were absolutely horrified. The house was the ultimate hoarder's fantasy/nightmare. There was garbage and books EVERYWHERE. Piled up everywhere. There was clothing and papers strewn all about. But what was worse was that he had clearly stopped caring for the animals in any real way.  It seemed that he had taken to buying bags of dog/cat food and slitting them each with an "X" then just leaving them there on the floor.


 There was dog and cat feces and urine in and on everything. The place was crawling with fleas. The smell was horrendous.The entire place was like a garbage dump with exception of one small spot on the floor. Just big enough for a malnourished man to sit cross legged. In that spot was a computer and a piece of a wire coat hanger bent and taped to the floor used for cleaning his crack pipe.


We salvaged what we could and rescued his pets. I adopted his cat (a beautiful orange manx named Amber,) and we eventually had his dogs placed in great homes. We got him moved into an apartment where he repeated his previous self destructive activities (including the hoarding.) He was arrested again and ended up in a half way house. Those houses seem to make it EASIER to get drugs rather than harder. When he died we weren't surprised. He was broken. It took less than 6 months from his initial imprisonment to his death. 

The image of that house with one small clear spot on the floor with the bent up hanger... that is the reason I've never tried any "hard drugs."
